title: The U.S. Senate Just Got a Lot Younger
gist: The 2026 midterms produced the biggest U.S. Senate turnover in nearly 50 years, with at least 15 new senators averaging about 55 years old replacing departing members averaging 70. That cuts the chamber's average age from 65.4 to at least 62.8, still above OECD peers, and nearly doubles the number of senators under 50.
